Founded in 1977 as the Senior Care Action Network, SCAN began with a simple but radical idea: that older adults deserve to stay healthy and independent. That belief was championed by a group of community activists we still honor today as the “12 Angry Seniors.” Their mission continues to guide everything we do.


Today, SCAN is a nonprofit health organization serving more than 500,000 people across Arizona, California, Nevada, New Mexico, Texas, and Washington, with over $8 billion in annual revenue. With nearly five decades of experience, we have built a distinctive, values\-driven platform dedicated to improving care for older adults.


Our work spans Medicare Advantage, fully integrated care models, primary care, care for the most medically and socially complex populations, and next\-generation care delivery models. Across all of this, we are united by a shared commitment: combining compassion with discipline, innovation with stewardship, and growth with integrity.


At SCAN, we believe scale should strengthen—not dilute—our mission. We are building the future of care for older adults, grounded in purpose, accountability, and respect for the people and communities we serve.

**Meeting Support Specialist:** Collect and prepare draft agendas, prioritize items in consultation with executives, finalize agendas, disseminate meeting materials, coordinate meeting records, evaluations, and follow\-up reports.

**Community of Practice Leader:** Lead and facilitate a community of practice with other executive assistants. Foster collaboration, share best practices, and promote professional development among peers.

**Office Management Maestro:** Assist with the administration of the executive office Board calendar and events, ensuring an organized, efficient, and welcoming work environment.

**Brand Management Ambassador:** Ensure consistent and cohesive brand representation internally and externally.

* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
* Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (including CoPilot).

**GHJ is looking for a** **High Net Worth (HNW) Tax Managing Director**


**WHY we get up in the morning**



At GHJ, we foster a flexible, entrepreneurial environment so our people achieve their personal and professional goals.



Our success is driven by retaining the best, diverse talent. We invest in our people and technology to deepen firm expertise and fuel sustainable growth. And we partner with our clients locally and globally to deliver innovative solutions.


**WHAT we believe**



GHJ works side by side with business leaders and nonprofit organizations to deliver responsive, high\-impact advisory, tax and accounting solutions that drive real results. Headquartered in Los Angeles with offices in Buffalo, Denver, Orange County and San Jose and backed by our own dispersed workforce, GHJ meets clients where they are to help leaders achieve their strategic goals.


**THRIVING On Our Own Terms**



We are deeply committed to our core values of Bright Minds, Brave Hearts and Bold Actions and incorporate them into every aspect of our business. By living these values, GHJ measures success by the strength of our relationships, the quality of our impact and the integrity of our actions. The Firm’s independence allows us to make strategic choices to innovate, invest and evolve with purpose. Ultimately, GHJ values operational excellence, financial discipline and the courage to prioritize sustainability over size.


**Summary of Role:**

GHJ is seeking an accomplished High Net Worth (HNW) Tax professional with deep experience in serving high net worth individuals and their related entities.



This position reports to the Tax Department Practice Leader.



The Tax HNW Managing Director will be responsible for leading client engagements requiring individual, trust and gift tax expertise. The ideal candidate will have advanced technical skills in a variety of tax areas, along with well\-developed and demonstrated management and supervisory skills. Administrative, leadership, and business development responsibilities are also key elements for this position.


### **You will be responsible for:**



The Tax HNW Managing Director is responsible for the efficient, accurate, complete, and timely preparation of all clients' tax returns whether prepared personally or by supervision of others. Advanced technical skills in a variety of tax and accounting areas, along with well\-developed and applied management and supervisory skills, are required. Responsibilities include:


* Managing the preparation and review of individual, trust and gift tax returns for high net worth individuals and their families;
* Performing technical tax review and approval of all tax returns of any complexity;
* Participating in client meetings and tax planning efforts for a variety of clients;
* Acting as a resource for tax preparers/specialists on specific tax issues and/or questions;
* Communicating to the appropriate firm personnel important tax and tax developments affecting the firm's clients;
* Managing governmental tax examinations; may represent the client before the appropriate taxing authorities;
* Supervising tax staff and providing on\-the\-job training;
* Working to develop responsible, trained staff by assisting in recruiting, performance evaluations, developing training aids, and acting as an instructor in professional development programs;
* Maintaining a knowledge of general economic and political trends of possible tax or other legislation that could affect the business climate;
* Participating in firm's practice development efforts through involvement with referral sources, community and industry activities.
### **What we need from you:**


* 10\+ years of experience in public accounting (tax), demonstrating a proven ability in handling tax complexity, scope, and research.
* Prior leadership of client engagements and supervisory experience of managers and staff.
* Required exposure to Forms 1040 (Individual return), 1041 (trust return), 1065 (partnership/LLC return), 1120S (S corporation return), and 709 (gift return).
* Experience with forms 5227 (Split Interest Trust Information return) and 706 (Estate return) would be a plus.
* Excellent oral \& written communication skills.
* Self\-starter with the ability to work independently and use good judgment.
* Strong interpersonal skills
* Creative thinker with entrepreneurial approach to client interactions, including tax planning and bringing value to clients.
* Willingness to lead firm or tax department initiatives and be seen as a leader in the tax department.
### **What skills \& experience you’ll bring to us:**


* Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Business, or related equivalent.
* Masters of Science degree in Taxation or a J.D. highly preferred
* CPA certification or active law license required.


**Seven decades, one enduring focus: our people and our clients.**



GHJ is a national independent advisory, tax and accounting firm that partners with businesses and nonprofit organizations to deliver clarity and confidence. Since 1953, GHJ has combined deep industry expertise with an entrepreneurial spirit to help leaders achieve their strategic goals.



GHJ is headquartered in Los Angeles and serves clients nationwide, backed by its own dispersed workforce. With nearly 300 professionals and 25\+ partners, the Firm provides senior\-level expertise with deep industry capabilities in food and beverage, media and advertising, entertainment and nonprofit.



GHJ is a top\-ranking firm in the U.S. and member of HLB International. Through this global network, GHJ offers seamless access to resources in over 150 countries while remaining fiercely focused on client success.

jobs.description:
### **About Teneo**


Teneo is the global CEO advisory firm. We partner with our clients globally to do great things for a better future.


Drawing upon our global team and expansive network of senior advisors, we provide advisory services across our five business segments on a stand\-alone or fully integrated basis to help our clients solve complex business challenges. Our clients include a significant number of the Fortune 100 and FTSE 100, as well as other corporations, financial institutions and organizations.


Our full range of advisory services includes strategic communications, investor relations, financial transactions and restructuring, management consulting, physical and cyber risk, organizational design, board and executive search, geopolitics and government affairs, corporate governance and ESG.


The firm has more than 1,800 employees located in 50\+ offices around the world.


### **The Opportunity**


Teneo's San Francisco office is in a building phase. We are assembling a small, senior team of advisors who understand how technology companies actually work: their customers, investors, boards, and regulators, and the internal dynamics their leaders have to navigate. We help these companies through moments of significant transition. The Managing Director will work with the San Francisco Office head to lead the office's Strategy \& Communications team, own a portfolio of client relationships, and play a central role in growing the office's business and reputation in the Bay Area. This is a chance to help shape an office and a practice, not just step into one.


We are also looking for someone who believes the communications function itself is changing. Our clients are rethinking what communications means inside their companies: how it connects to strategy, how it is structured and staffed, and how new tools, including AI, are changing the work. We want an MD who can help clients lead that evolution and who is eager to help Teneo do the same.


### **Who We're Looking For**


The strongest candidates will be builders. Many will have held senior in\-house roles at technology companies, where they built or rebuilt teams, processes, and systems, and learned to advise across internal silos because they had to operate inside them. We equally value agency and advisory leaders who have built something of their own, such as a practice, an office, or a new offering, and who bring real empathy for the operator's seat. Either way, you understand that good counsel starts with knowing a client's world, not just the outcome they want.


### **Responsibilities**


* Work with the San Francisco Office Head to lead the San Francisco Strategy \& Communications team. Set direction, develop talent, provide senior\-level oversight across engagements, and help recruit the people who will grow the office.
* Serve as a trusted advisor to founders, CEOs, and senior leaders, influencing client direction and building long\-term relationships.
* Drive business development. Originate new client relationships, expand existing ones, and turn the office's network into client work.
* Help clients through moments of transition, including fundraising, IPO readiness, leadership changes, M\&A, regulatory scrutiny, crises, and shifts in business model or technology. Translate the realities of a technology business for the audiences that judge it.
* Develop and lead complex, integrated communications programs that use every lever together: earned media, owned and social channels, executive visibility, events, and non\-traditional media such as podcasts, newsletters, and online video.
* Advise clients on how their communications function should evolve, including its structure, capabilities, operating model, and use of new tools.
* Build Teneo's presence in the Bay Area through thought leadership, signature events, speaking, and relationships across the technology, investor, and business communities.
* Partner with colleagues across Teneo's segments, including management consulting, investor relations, financial advisory, risk, and executive search, to deliver integrated solutions.
* Help the office experiment with and adopt AI\-enabled ways of working, in partnership with Teneo's firmwide AI efforts.
* Make complex decisions affecting colleagues and clients in a timely and transparent way, and foster a culture where quality and client satisfaction come first.

### **Qualifications**


* 15\+ years of relevant experience in corporate communications, public relations, media, or a related field.
* A track record of building teams, functions, practices, processes, or systems, ideally including leading an organization through significant transformation.
* Senior in\-house communications experience at a technology company is strongly preferred. Agency and advisory leaders with deep technology\-client experience are also encouraged to apply.
* Significant experience independently leading large, complex client engagements.
* Experience counseling senior executives and boards, and working alongside external financial and legal advisors.
* Deep familiarity with the technology ecosystem, particularly founders of mid\- to late\-stage startups, with strong relationships across both traditional and non\-traditional media.
* A holistic view of communications as a driver of business outcomes.
* Curiosity about AI and hands\-on use of AI tools in your own work.
* Comfort with ambiguity and the pace of building something new.
* Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
* Available to work from Teneo's San Francisco office at least three days a week.
* Experience in technology, media, or fintech, especially mid\- to late\-stage startups and newly public companies preferred.

  

**What We Offer**


As a Teneo employee, you will enjoy unique benefits including flexible time off policy; medical, dental, and vision coverage; long\-term disability, and life insurance; a 401K plan; commuter benefits; team events; snacks; and other perks

**JOB DESCRIPTION**  

  

  

Chase Card Services is seeking a visionary, commercially driven executive to drive the Authorized User (AU) business as a standalone growth engine across the Sapphire, Freedom, and Slate portfolios. Today's cardmembers increasingly manage spending across families, partners, and trusted individuals. The next generation of AU experiences will be powered by a dynamic lineup of card choices, real\-time spend controls, personalized benefits and rewards, and enhanced servicing experiences that make every Authorized User feel like a primary cardmember relationship.  



  

Create customer\-first Authorized User experiences that help people confidently manage shared spending across families and trusted individuals. **About HARC**

HARC is a private 501(c)(3\) nonprofit agricultural research organization headquartered at the Kunia Research Station in Waipahu, Oʻahu. Its team of scientists, agronomists, foresters, conservationists, and technical experts works across five core research divisions. jobs.description:
UVC is seeking its next Chief Executive Officer to lead the organization's continued growth and impact. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the CEO will be responsible for UVC's strategy, fundraising, external relationships, team, and financial sustainability. This is a highly external, entrepreneurial role for someone who can build relationships, raise resources, connect people, and identify opportunities to strengthen entrepreneurship across Upstate New York.


*Prior nonprofit experience is not required. Experience as a founder, investor, business leader, fundraiser, or ecosystem builder may be equally relevant.*

**About UVC**  

Founded in 2010 by entrepreneurs, Upstate Venture Connect (UVC) is a 501c3 nonprofit working to build a more connected, entrepreneur\-led economy across Upstate New York. UVC supports founders building high\-growth, venture\-backable companies by helping them access the relationships, experience, capital, customers, talent, and other resources they need to scale while remaining in the region.


UVC serves as the connective tissue among Upstate New York’s regional startup communities. Our Founder Network is free to join and provides entrepreneurs with personalized introductions to other founders, investors, experienced operators, mentors, advisors, corporate partners, and potential customers. UVC is tracking more than 800 high\-growth companies across Upstate NY and facilitates more than 550 curated introductions for them every year. Its broader network includes more than 18,000 contacts and startup supporters. (More info: UVC 2025 Annual Report)


UVC’s Community Advocate network provides a locally based presence across Upstate New York. Community Advocates act as regional connectors, scouts, and champions. They identify and engage founders, organize local gatherings, build partnerships, make strategic introductions, and connect entrepreneurs in their communities to UVC’s nationwide network. This model allows UVC to strengthen individual startup communities while connecting founders to opportunities beyond their immediate region.


At the center of UVC is the UNY50 Leadership Network, an invitation\-only group of accomplished entrepreneurs, executives, and business leaders committed to giving back. UNY50 members volunteer their time, experience, and networks to help emerging founders navigate the challenges of building and scaling companies. The majority are also active early\-stage investors.


UVC hosts more than 20 curated events per year. Its programming centers on four types of gatherings: regional Office Hours, which give founders access to personalized feedback from UNY50 members, investors, and mentors; multi\-day Founder Roadshows, which connect select Upstate companies with investors, customers, and entrepreneurial networks in major markets like NYC, Boston and Washington, DC; curated founder and leadership dinners, designed to build trusted relationships among experienced and emerging entrepreneurs; and Unleashed, UVC’s annual invitation\-only founders retreat. These programs create opportunities for meaningful connections that can help founders access capital, customers, talent, mentorship, and other resources needed to scale.


UVC’s work is funded through foundation support, corporate sponsorships, individual donations, and program revenue. Its impact is also made possible by a statewide community of corporate and community partners, universities, financial institutions, investors, board members, advisors, volunteers, and founders who share a commitment to creating more high\-growth opportunities in Upstate New York. (UVC Partners)

**Key Responsibilities**

* Fundraising \& Growth: Own UVC's fundraising and revenue strategy with a goal towards long term financial sustainability. Build and maintain relationships with corporations, foundations, financial institutions, government partners, donors, and sponsors.
* Network \& Partnerships: Build and maintain relationships with founders, investors, executives, universities, economic development organizations, and other partners across New York State and beyond.
* Ecosystem Leadership: Serve as a visible ambassador for UVC and Upstate NY’s entrepreneurial community; grow and engage the regionwide network, and connect founders to capital, customers, talent, mentors, and other opportunities.
* Strategy, Operations \& Leadership: Set organizational priorities with the Board and lead their execution. Develop and oversee the annual budget that balances strategic goals with the resources available to the organization. Manage UVC's team and financial resources to support the strategy and stay compliant with regulatory requirements. Oversee the Community Advocate network and execution of UVC's programs and gatherings, and identify new opportunities for partnerships, programs, and growth.

  

**Requirements** **The Ideal Candidate will have**

* A strong affinity for UVC's mission and entrepreneurship in Upstate New York
* Demonstrated success building relationships, partnerships, and networks
* Experience fundraising, generating revenue, developing and managing to a budget, selling, or securing financial support from individual donors, corporate sponsors, foundations and/or government sources
* An entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to move between strategy and hands\-on execution
* Credibility with founders, investors, business leaders, funders, and community partners
* Strong communication and public speaking skills
* Comfort with emerging tech including use of AI
* Experience leading a team, managing a budget, and driving organizational priorities


This position has a base salary of $110,000\-$130,000 plus opportunity for incentive compensation

 **Benefits**  

We offer a comprehensive suite of benefits including health insurance coverage and 401K savings accounts.

**Job Title:** Advancement Director, West
**Department:** Advancement
**Location:** Remote (preferred within the Pacific Northwest)

This position requires an ability to travel.
**Reports To:** Managing Director, Major Gifts, West  


**Context**: At the Sierra Club, we believe in the power of interdependence. Together, we remain committed to the fight for a healthy climate built on a foundation of environmental, racial, economic, and gender justice – a future where all people benefit from a healthy, thriving planet and a direct connection to nature. As the climate crisis and deeply entrenched systemic racism all fuel injustice, we will continue to fight for a bold, transformational agenda that recognizes the interconnectedness between our planet, our humanity, and our future. By recognizing that our destinies are tied, we continue to name that all things are fundamentally connected, and the overlap between ecology, race, gender, and representative government will move to either advance our collective humanity or to oppress it. Sierra Club has close to 700 staff across the country and a network of 64 local chapters that are led and fueled by thousands of volunteers. We are also proud to be a unionized employer, with three labor unions representing more than half of our employees.  


**Scope:** This is an opportunity to join the Advancement team of the country’s leading grassroots environmental organization. At a critical time for the planet, Sierra Club is running highly effective campaigns to address climate change, protect wilderness and wildlife, and advance these priorities by rooting the work in justice and equity for all. We are seeking an Advancement Director responsible for identifying, cultivating, and soliciting gifts of $25,000 and greater. In this position, you will be part of a dynamic team of gift officers raising upwards of $65 million dollars annually for our high\-impact campaigns from individual donors, family foundations, and institutional funders within the defined geographic region. The Advancement Director will engage donors and prospects throughout the region via discovery, cultivation, engagement, solicitation and stewardship activities. Valid driver’s license, satisfactory driving record, and proof of auto insurance required. 40\-50% of travel is typically expected in this role.
### **Job activities include but are not limited to:**



* **Portfolio Management**
	+ Personally manages a portfolio of high\-potential prospects and donors by identifying and cultivating new prospects.
	+ Engages with prospects and donors through face\-to\-face meetings, phone, video conference, digital engagements, and writing based on a clear strategy for cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
	+ Solicits assigned donors for gifts of $25,000 and more to meet organizational priorities and annual projected fundraising revenue goals.
	+ In collaboration with the Sr. Managing Director, Chief Advancement Officer (CAO) and other Advancement Team members, identifies and pursues new prospects, developing and implementing a clear strategy for each prospect, leading to new and increased giving over time by connecting donor philanthropic priorities with Sierra Club’s programs and priorities.
	+ Leverages donor engagement events in the West and Northwest geographic regions to identify, cultivate and solicit new and existing prospects and donors.
	+ Prepares and sends donor correspondence, including written solicitations and proposals.
	+ Develops and maintains an in\-depth knowledge of the organization’s activities, priorities and needs. Applies this knowledge in matching the interests and needs of prospective donors with the strategic needs of the organization and campaigns.
	+ Captures all interactions and relationships in the donor database in a timely manner. 30%\-40% travel is likely for this role with travel occurring across the country.
* **Strategic Planning and Execution**
	+ Drives strategies and plans to identify, cultivate, upgrade and/or solicit new donors, with an eye towards building a strong pipeline of qualified major donors and high\-net\-worth individuals with the capacity to give $25,000 or greater.
	+ Maintain knowledge and expertise in environmental issues broadly, including climate change, clean energy, land, water and wildlife conservation. Work with Campaign and Chapter key staff and teams to help develop and implement relevant major gift programs, initiatives, events, and materials.
### **The successful candidate must demonstrate the following skills, experience and competencies:**


* Senior\-level, extensive experience, equivalent combination of experience and education in development and major gift fundraising, including a strong background in the identification, qualification and cultivation and solicitation of six and higher figure gifts to nonprofit organizations or similar equivalent experience.
* Proven ability and inclination to build a portfolio of prospects and grow a revenue pipeline through active identification, qualification and cultivation strategies
* Strong knowledge of fundraising best practices, planned giving, financial and/or estate planning concepts, and campaign planning.
* Personal success identifying, qualifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding individual and institutional donors at the major and principal gifts levels, and ability to inspire high\-net\-worth individuals and institutional funders to provide significant financial support to an organization.
* Deep understanding of and appreciation for the philanthropic process and individual giving behaviors.
* Experience working with organizational leadership, preferably in a non\-profit setting.
* Ability to develop strong, positive, and constructive relationships with internal and external stakeholders; high emotional intelligence and flexibility, with the ability to continually experiment, learn, and revise strategies; and the exceptional ability to juggle a heavy volume of div

jobs.description:
**Job Summary**

.Safe Haven of Greater Waterbury, the state\-designated domestic violence organization serving the Greater Waterbury region, is seeking an experienced, visionary, and collaborative **Executive Director** to lead the organization in advancing its mission of providing safety, support, advocacy, and healing to victims and survivors of domestic and sexual violence.

For nearly five decades, Safe Haven has been a trusted resource in the Greater Waterbury community. The organization provides a comprehensive continuum of services, including a 24\-hour crisis hotline, emergency shelter, rapid rehousing and housing advocacy, lethality and risk assessment, legal advocacy, hospital accompaniment, counseling, advocacy, services for children and families, prevention education, and other supportive services. Safe Haven is a member of the Connecticut Coalition Against Domestic Violence (CCADV) and the Connecticut Alliance to End Sexual Violence (The Alliance).

The Opportunity

The Executive Director serves as Safe Haven's chief executive and administrative officer and is responsible for the organization's overall leadership, administration, financial health, operational integrity, program effectiveness, personnel, fund development, community relationships, and public presence.

Working closely with the Board of Directors and staff, the Executive Director translates the organization's mission and strategic priorities into effective programs, sound operations, responsible fiscal management, and measurable community impact.

This is a hands\-on executive leadership role requiring the ability to balance long\-term strategy with day\-to\-day management, respond effectively to complex and time\-sensitive situations, and maintain a strong commitment to trauma\-informed, survivor\-centered, culturally responsive, and confidential services.

Key ResponsibilitiesExecutive Leadership \& Organizational Management

* Provide overall leadership and direction for the organization and ensure operations align with the mission, strategic plan, policies, and Board directives.
* Develop and implement organizational goals, priorities, policies, procedures, and operational plans.
* Identify emerging organizational, community, regulatory, and service\-delivery needs and develop appropriate responses.
* Foster an organizational culture that is trauma\-informed, survivor\-centered, equitable, ethical, professional, and respectful.
* Represent Safe Haven in community, professional, governmental, coalition, and public settings.

Financial Management \& Fiscal Oversight

* Maintain overall responsibility for the financial management and fiscal integrity of the organization.
* Develop and monitor the annual organizational budget in partnership with staff and the Board.
* Monitor revenues, expenditures, cash flow, restricted and unrestricted funds, and overall financial performance.
* Review and use financial reports to inform operational decisions, resource allocation, staffing, program development, and organizational sustainability.
* Work closely with the organization's accountant and financial professionals to ensure accurate financial reporting and reconciliation of budgets to actual expenditures.
* Ensure grant expenditures are accurate, allowable, appropriately allocated, adequately documented, and consistent with approved grant budgets and funding requirements.
* Oversee audits, tax filings, financial reporting, and other required fiscal submissions.
* Identify financial risks and opportunities and develop strategies to support long\-term sustainability.

Grants, Contracts \& Fund Development

* Lead the organization's overall grant development and funding strategy.
* Identify, pursue, and secure public and private funding opportunities.
* Develop, write, and submit grant applications, proposals, renewals, and other funding requests.
* Oversee the organization's portfolio of grants, contracts, and funding agreements.
* Ensure grant and contract deliverables, reporting requirements, budgets, and performance measures are appropriately managed.
* Cultivate relationships with government agencies, foundations, corporations, donors, and other funding partners.
* Develop and implement fundraising and resource\-development strategies in partnership with staff and the Board.
* Support major fundraising events, donor cultivation, sponsorships, and stewardship.
* Pursue diversified revenue opportunities to strengthen long\-term financial sustainability.

Program Leadership \& Quality Assurance

* Provide executive oversight of Safe Haven's programs and services, including emergency shelter, crisis intervention, advocacy, counseling, housing, legal advocacy, prevention, and related services.
* Ensure services effectively address the needs of victims and survivors and reflect evidence\-informed and trauma\-informed practices.
* Monitor program performance, outcomes, utilization, service demand, and emerging community needs.
* Ensure programs meet applicable contractual, regulatory, and funding requirements.
* Promote quality improvement, program coordination, innovation, and responsible growth.
* Protect client confidentiality, safety, dignity, and rights.

Emergency Shelter, Safety \& Risk Management

* Provide executive oversight of Safe Haven's confidential\-location emergency shelter and crisis\-response operations.
* Ensure shelter operations are safe, secure, appropriately staffed, trauma\-informed, and responsive to residents and their families.
* Oversee emergency preparedness, continuity\-of\-operations, security, incident response, workplace safety, cybersecurity, insurance, and other organizational risk\-management practices.

new_jobs.title: CEO - Upstate Venture Connect
new_jobs.description:
UVC is seeking its next Chief Executive Officer to lead the organization's continued growth and impact. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the CEO will be responsible for UVC's strategy, fundraising, external relationships, team, and financial sustainability. This is a highly external, entrepreneurial role for someone who can build relationships, raise resources, connect people, and identify opportunities to strengthen entrepreneurship across Upstate New York.


*Prior nonprofit experience is not required. Experience as a founder, investor, business leader, fundraiser, or ecosystem builder may be equally relevant.*

**About UVC**  

Founded in 2010 by entrepreneurs, Upstate Venture Connect (UVC) is a 501c3 nonprofit working to build a more connected, entrepreneur\-led economy across Upstate New York. UVC supports founders building high\-growth, venture\-backable companies by helping them access the relationships, experience, capital, customers, talent, and other resources they need to scale while remaining in the region.


UVC serves as the connective tissue among Upstate New York’s regional startup communities. Our Founder Network is free to join and provides entrepreneurs with personalized introductions to other founders, investors, experienced operators, mentors, advisors, corporate partners, and potential customers. UVC is tracking more than 800 high\-growth companies across Upstate NY and facilitates more than 550 curated introductions for them every year. Its broader network includes more than 18,000 contacts and startup supporters. (More info: UVC 2025 Annual Report)


UVC’s Community Advocate network provides a locally based presence across Upstate New York. Community Advocates act as regional connectors, scouts, and champions. They identify and engage founders, organize local gatherings, build partnerships, make strategic introductions, and connect entrepreneurs in their communities to UVC’s nationwide network. This model allows UVC to strengthen individual startup communities while connecting founders to opportunities beyond their immediate region.


At the center of UVC is the UNY50 Leadership Network, an invitation\-only group of accomplished entrepreneurs, executives, and business leaders committed to giving back. UNY50 members volunteer their time, experience, and networks to help emerging founders navigate the challenges of building and scaling companies. The majority are also active early\-stage investors.


UVC hosts more than 20 curated events per year. Its programming centers on four types of gatherings: regional Office Hours, which give founders access to personalized feedback from UNY50 members, investors, and mentors; multi\-day Founder Roadshows, which connect select Upstate companies with investors, customers, and entrepreneurial networks in major markets like NYC, Boston and Washington, DC; curated founder and leadership dinners, designed to build trusted relationships among experienced and emerging entrepreneurs; and Unleashed, UVC’s annual invitation\-only founders retreat. These programs create opportunities for meaningful connections that can help founders access capital, customers, talent, mentorship, and other resources needed to scale.


UVC’s work is funded through foundation support, corporate sponsorships, individual donations, and program revenue. Its impact is also made possible by a statewide community of corporate and community partners, universities, financial institutions, investors, board members, advisors, volunteers, and founders who share a commitment to creating more high\-growth opportunities in Upstate New York. (UVC Partners)

**Key Responsibilities**

* Fundraising \& Growth: Own UVC's fundraising and revenue strategy with a goal towards long term financial sustainability. Build and maintain relationships with corporations, foundations, financial institutions, government partners, donors, and sponsors.
* Network \& Partnerships: Build and maintain relationships with founders, investors, executives, universities, economic development organizations, and other partners across New York State and beyond.
* Ecosystem Leadership: Serve as a visible ambassador for UVC and Upstate NY’s entrepreneurial community; grow and engage the regionwide network, and connect founders to capital, customers, talent, mentors, and other opportunities.
* Strategy, Operations \& Leadership: Set organizational priorities with the Board and lead their execution. Develop and oversee the annual budget that balances strategic goals with the resources available to the organization. Manage UVC's team and financial resources to support the strategy and stay compliant with regulatory requirements. Oversee the Community Advocate network and execution of UVC's programs and gatherings, and identify new opportunities for partnerships, programs, and growth.

  

**Requirements** **The Ideal Candidate will have**

* A strong affinity for UVC's mission and entrepreneurship in Upstate New York
* Demonstrated success building relationships, partnerships, and networks
* Experience fundraising, generating revenue, developing and managing to a budget, selling, or securing financial support from individual donors, corporate sponsors, foundations and/or government sources
* An entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to move between strategy and hands\-on execution
* Credibility with founders, investors, business leaders, funders, and community partners
* Strong communication and public speaking skills
* Comfort with emerging tech including use of AI
* Experience leading a team, managing a budget, and driving organizational priorities

 **Benefits**  

We offer a comprehensive suite of benefits including health insurance coverage and 401K savings accounts.
